subject: Skyline perf follow-up: A/B tests and lab plan
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-27T09:12:00Z
Subject: Skyline call recap + immediate asks

Team — quick recap from this morning's discovery with Sara / Skyline engineering (30m):

Summary:
- Skyline is evaluating inference providers for a new customer-facing summarization API (short inputs, bursts of traffic).
- Their two shortlists: HyperscalerX (managed endpoints) and Redwood. Primary concerns: p95/p99 latency, cold-start microbursts (tokens/sec), and consistent tail latency under batching.
- They want an apples-to-apples A/B run across 2 workloads: conversational prompts (avg 120 tokens) and short summarize (avg 40 tokens).

What they asked for (actionable):
1) A/B test spec for latency (p50/p95/p99) and sustained tokens/sec (60s windows).
2) Workload payloads + header capture for identical client-side conditions.
3) Suggested test configs: single-shot low-latency route (no batching), small-batch (batch size 8), and cache-enabled prefix test.
4) Timeline: Skyline wants first lab results within 7 business days.

Proposed Redwood approach (short):
- Run parallel tests on Shield (dedicated) and Hosted (standard) to show variance.
- Compare against HyperscalerX results (Skyline will run their side; they asked us to run an independent Redwood side).
- Key metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, failed requests rate, and cost per 1k tokens.

Immediate asks for the team:
- Marissa: can you convert the outline into a one-page runbook and an XLS with the exact payloads + measurement harness? (attachment: skyline_probe_runbook.xlsx)
- Rishi: can infra spin up a dedicated small pool (2x A100 equiv) for short window tests and enable KV cache? Need ETA and any special config notes.
- Ben: handle procurement/contract signal — if results show favorable tail, we should be ready to fast-track a POC engagement (terms + reserved capacity).

I'll draft the external note to Sara once we have the runbook and infra ETA.

Thanks — Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2027-07-27T10:08:00Z
Subject: Re: Skyline call recap + immediate asks

Thanks — good notes. I started a skeleton runbook and attached the initial XLS with payload buckets and expected metrics (skyline_probe_runbook.xlsx). A few clarifications: 

- For the small-batch config I'll include both static batch-size=8 and an adaptive-batching mode we use in Dedicated (so Skyline sees both).
- For tokens/sec, we'll capture both observed tokens/s and effective tokens/s (post-batching) so we can compare how batching impacts client vs server metrics.
- I'll add a short section on measuring microbursts: 10-second sliding windows inside the 60s sustained window.

ETA: Runbook + payloads v1 by EOD today. Will also include run commands and the measurement script (node/python stubs).

Marissa
Product Ops — Performance Labs

Subject: Skyline perf follow-up: A/B tests and lab plan

Sara — thanks again for the time this morning. Per our call here is a concise plan to validate tail latency and sustained throughput against HyperscalerX.

Plan highlights:
- Tests: conversational (120t), short-summarize (40t) across three server configs: low-latency (no batching), fixed-batch (size=8), dedicated adaptive-batch.
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec (60s windows + 10s microbursts), error rate, and cost/1k tokens.
- Who runs what: Skyline to run HyperscalerX side using the shared payloads. Redwood will run Hosted + Dedicated side. We'll align start times for identical client workload timing.
- Timeline: deliver initial results within 7 business days after runbook sign-off.

Next steps (action items):
- Marissa: deliver runbook + payload XLS (attached) by EOD today.
- Rishi: provide infra ETA for dedicated pool (estimated start: 48 hours after sign-off).
- Ben: share POC commercial brief once we have initial numbers.
- Sara: please confirm you can run the HyperscalerX side and share any constraints (eg region, IP allowlist).

Attachments: skyline_probe_runbook.xlsx, sample_payloads.json (links provided)

Scheduling: here's a quick scheduling link for an alignment checkpoint once runbook is posted — https://cal.com/redwood/30m (pick any slot next week).
